# Consistency audit

Whether a message architecture's pillars are actually being said the same way across reps and channels weeks after it was written — the sustainment audit's shape, applied to messaging instead of a kaizen event.

Family: Standard work · Format: .xlsx · Domain: commercial

## What it is

A message architecture written once and never checked again drifts, the same way any standard does — a rep rounds a number up, marketing gets ahead of the evidence, an unproven pillar quietly becomes a headline claim. This audit is the sustainment audit's exact shape, applied to a message architecture: restate what it was supposed to ensure, get a checklist of specific, verifiable practices, and see honestly which are still holding.

## When to use it

Use it when:

- A message architecture has been live long enough to check whether reps and channels are actually still using it consistently, not just whether it was written.
- You want to catch message drift — a claim getting ahead of its actual proof, or each channel restating a number differently — before it becomes the norm.
- You want to close a gap the message architecture itself flagged when it was first built (a pillar deliberately held back as unproven).

Not when:

- The message architecture was just published — give it real time in market before auditing it.

## How to fill it in

- **originalObjective** — What was the message architecture supposed to ensure — which pillars, in what language?
- **checks** — Drafted from what the message architecture was supposed to ensure — verify what's actually still holding across reps and channels.
- **narrative** — Drafted from the checklist actually built.

## What good looks like

The example below audits the Beacon Analytics message architecture sixty days after it was published — including whether the pillar it deliberately held back as unproven has stayed out of real marketing claims, and finding a real drift where it hasn't.

Full worked example, on-screen and as a downloadable .xlsx: https://www.katafacts.com/katas/consistency-audit

## Common mistakes

- **Auditing a message architecture that was never actually rolled out to reps or channels.** — This audit checks whether real usage has drifted from a real standard — there's nothing to check if the message was never actually put into use.
- **Marking a practice as holding without actually checking the live sales deck, site copy, or a real call.** — The audit only has value if it reflects what's actually being said, not a hopeful assumption that the message architecture is being followed.

## What it connects to

Upstream:

- **Message architecture** — The architecture's own pillars and proof points are exactly what this audit checks against reality — including whether an unproven pillar has quietly crept into claims anyway.

## Where AI helps

Judgement — stays with you:

- Deciding how much time to give a message architecture in market before auditing it
- Deciding what to do about a pillar that's drifted from its proven language

Analysis — AI helps:

- Drafting specific, verifiable checks from a description of what the message architecture was supposed to ensure
- Drafting the narrative from the checklist actually built

Drudgery — automated:

- Tallying how many practices are still holding
- Identifying which practices are at risk
- Exporting to xlsx in the house format
